# minimaxflash-1.4 — the level mapped to two thirds, and the staircase not in it

*Model: `minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, played by opencode. A
carry-on of `minimaxflash-1.3`, which stopped alive on depth 1 at ask 609.*

*Files I opened before playing: `CONTINUEGAME.txt` (all), `AGENTS.md`,
`docs/BRIEF.md` (all), `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` (all), my own playbook
`agents/minimax/COMMON.md` (all) and `agents/minimax/DRUID.md` (all), my own
three write-ups `runs/minimaxflash-1/REPORT.md`,
`runs/minimaxflash-1.2/REPORT.md` and `runs/minimaxflash-1.3/REPORT.md`,
the inherited notebook `runs/minimaxflash-1.4/notebook.md` (106 lines),
`tools/screen/{map,look,explore}.py`, and in `vendor/angband/` the source and
data I needed for the questions I had: `src/player-path.c`, `src/mon-util.c`,
`src/obj-make.c`, `src/trap.c`, `src/ui-target.c`, `src/cmd-cave.c`,
`src/cave.c`, `src/cave-view.c`, `src/cave-square.c`, `src/gen-util.c`,
`src/player-calcs.c`, `src/ui-display.c`, `src/ui-map.c`, `src/player-util.c`,
`lib/gamedata/{monster,monster_base,object,trap}.txt`. NOT read: any other
run's decisions, report or notebook, `PLAN.md`, `ACCUMULATED_KNOWLEDGE.md`,
or the `knowledge/` pages of other families.*

## What happened

**145 decisions, 2,656 keypresses, turn 17,281 to turn 24,105.** The
character came to life as a High-Elf Druid at character level 4 on depth 1 of
seed 23, with 33/33 hit points, 7/7 spell points, armour class 12, 3 gold, 21
flasks of oil, a Lesser Charms book with four spells, a torch and a cloak —
and **no potion, no escape scroll and no way home**, because the second life
of this character spent both Phase Door scrolls and read the Word of Recall.

This life spent all of its budget on one thing: **sweeping the level for
the one down staircase.** The result is a measured negative. **The sweep
mapped 130 of the level's 198 columns and all 66 rows — about 66 per cent of
its 13,068 squares — and there is no down staircase anywhere in it.** Three up
staircases were found (level 63/6, 149/18 and 139/57) and no down one. Seven
locked doors were opened, four chests were found and every one was empty, and
the character ended alive on depth 1 at **29/33 hit points**, level 4, with
**two experience units** gained in 145 decisions.

The character also came away better equipped than it started: a floor of
**four Potions of Cure Light Wounds**, nineteen flasks of oil and a
permanent light, none of which it had when I took over.

## The result that is worth something: the coverage measurement

My own notes had this as the standing open question — *"is the down
staircase findable at all by walking?"* — and the honest answer after this
life is a number rather than a yes or a no:

- **The level is 198 × 66** (`constants.txt`), about 13,068 squares.
- **The generator puts exactly one down staircase on it**, on a square with
  exactly three adjacent walls, drawn uniformly at random
  (`gen-util.c:620` `alloc_stairs`, `gen-cave.c:1583`). That makes it a dead
  end, and the level is full of dead ends, so there is no way to guess where.
- **This life mapped 130 columns × 66 rows** — level columns 50 to 180, rows
  0 to 63 — and found no `>` glyph in any of it. The M map was the
  instrument: it is the only view of the whole level at once, and it was
  checked after every ten decisions.
- The remaining 34 per cent is the western quarter of the level, and it is
  **not reachable from the eastern two thirds**: the corridor along the
  level's northern edge ends in a two-by-two pocket at column 78, and the
  level's southern rows are cut off from the middle by walls. The
  character finished at level column 50, the westernmost square any life
  of it has reached on this level, with fifty columns of level still
  black in front of it.

So: **the staircase is in the western quarter, and no amount of walking in
the eastern two thirds will find it.** That is a real result, and it is a
result about the *level*, not about the character.

## The findings, with their evidence

**1. The M map draws the WHOLE level, scaled down — my own notes said
otherwise for three lives.** `display_map` (`src/ui-map.c:761`) computes
`row = (y * map_hgt) / cave->height` and `col = (x * map_wid) /
cave->width` for **every square of the level**, so the M panel is a picture
of the entire 198 × 66 dungeon at 78 × 22, not a window into it. My
COMMON.md said "M is a window onto the level" and "M shows only the
remembered region"; the second half is right (it reads `cave->memory`, so
unexplored squares are blank) and the first half is wrong. The correction
matters: **M is the only way to know where you are on the level**, because
the main map panel scrolls and its rows are drawn behind the sidebar, so the
same square appears at a different column on different screens. I lost
several decisions to that (ask 683: I read a scroll as a teleport; ask 679
and ask 695: I read the panel shift as a walk in the wrong direction).

**2. Experience is divided by the player's level, so a character that
wants to level must go deeper — and going deeper needs the staircase.**
`player_kill_monster` (`src/mon-util.c:1082`) computes
`new_exp = (mon->race->mexp * mon->race->level) / p->lev`. On depth 1 at
character level 4 that is `mexp / 4`: a small kobold (5 exp) is **1.25
units**, a grey mould (3) is 0.75, a mushroom patch (1) is 0.25. Character
level 5 needs 28 units. **A depth-1 kill is worth a quarter of an
experience unit at level 4, so 23 kills is the cheapest possible route to
level 5, and no level-1 player will ever take it.** On depth 2 the same
formula gives `mexp * 2 / 4`, so a giant black ant is 4 units and Grip is
15. My three lives together earned 2 units. That is the whole reason the
earlier lives chased the staircase, and it is the reason this one did too —
and it is a fact none of us had written down.

**3. Lock picking has a formula, and a failed pick cancels the rest of
your key string.** `calc_unlocking_chance` (`src/player-calcs.c:1676`)
returns `MAX(2, skill - 4 * lock_power)`; the lock level is `randint1(7)`
(`src/gen-util.c:581`); a CL4 High-Elf Druid has `SKILL_DISARM_PHYS` =
30 (Druid) + 10 × 3 (levels) + 4 (High-Elf) = 64. So the chance is **36 to
60 per cent**, one attempt at a time — and on failure the game prints
*"You failed to pick the lock. Cancelled."*, which is the run-cancel
message: **the rest of the key string is eaten**. My notebook said
"Searching is 26 percent"; the source says 36 to 60. And a string of
repeated presses is useless against a lock: it is one attempt per ask.

**4. A picked lock does not move you.** Pressing into a locked door picks
the lock and leaves the character on the near side, so every locked door
costs two decisions: one to pick and one to step through. (Asks 619/624,
668/669, 696/697.) I lost two more to the other half of this: the escape
from the object context menu is `\e\e` — **`\ee` is Escape followed by the
letter `e`**, not two Escapes, and my trailing `g` re-selected the armour in
the equipment list and reopened the menu.

**5. Whether the aimed walk finds new ground depends on whether its
destination is known.** `find_path` (`src/player-path.c:1107`) sets
`only_known = square_isknown(start) && square_isknown(dest)`. An aim that
lands on a square you have already seen is pathed over remembered ground
only — a stroll along corridors you have walked. An aim that lands on a
square you have **not** seen is pathed through unknown ground, which the
pathfinder treats as passable, and the walk crosses new territory as it
goes. **So the rule is: aim further than the edge of what you know.** This
resolves the disagreement between my own lives two and three about the
same recipe.

**6. The aimed walk is a slot machine: it covers about seventeen tiles an
ask and its direction is not under the player's control.** Measured over
this life on the same recipe (`*`, forty-five direction digits, `g`): 0, 1,
1, 3, 9, 23, 24, 26, 32 and 33 tiles, and it went the wrong way about
half the time. The cursor clamps to the level bounds, so a big aim is a
request for the **edge** of the level in that direction, and the pathfinder
answers with whatever route it believes is cheapest. It is a good way to
cover ground and a bad way to go where you point.

**7. The look-mode walk is the navigator, and it is worth more than the
aimed walk.** In look mode a direction key does not move the cursor one
tile: it **snaps the cursor to the next interesting square** in that
direction — a door, a monster, an item or a staircase — and the message
line names it with its exact offset. So `l` + a direction + `g` walks you
along the corridor to the next door in one ask (six to twelve tiles, every
time), which on a level that is nothing but corridors and doors is the
cheapest way to move there is. `lxg` is the same idea with the frontier
instead of the next door: it advanced one tile per ask on this level, which
is why my notes called it slow.

**8. `!` is ambiguous in a text dump.** `object.txt` gives the oil kind
`graphics:!:y` **and** the potions `graphics:!:d`; only the colour tells
them apart, and a plain-text player never sees colour. What I picked up
expecting a flask of oil was **four Potions of Cure Light Wounds**. A
player who wants to know what a `!` is must look at it, because the map
cannot say.

**9. Every chest on this level is an empty one.** Four times I was told
*"You see nothing there to open"* — that is a chest with `pval` 0, which
`obj-chest.c` treats as not openable. Two chests in this life and two in
the earlier ones. **A chest on depth 1 of this level is not treasure, and
the two decisions spent on it would have been better spent walking.**

**10. A Scroll of Blessing lasts about thirty turns.** Reading it gave
armour class 17 and a whip that could reach armour class 36 (to-hit 29
against 36, where 19 could not), which killed a giant white centipede in
three swings instead of five. Then *"The prayer has expired."* A buff is a
minute of play on this level, not a plan.

**11. Gold drops on depth 1 average about seventeen.** `make_gold`
(`src/obj-make.c:1296`) averages `(16 * lev) / 10 + 16`. So the way to
buy a Magic Mapping scroll or a Phase Door is to kill things, and killing
on depth 1 at level 4 pays a quarter of an experience unit a kill. The
character had 3 gold and no way to earn more, which is the whole reason
this life was a sweep and not a shopping trip.

**12. The level is a lattice of corridors with a locked door at every third
segment, and it has three up staircases.** Seven locks opened in this life;
the corridors run east-west and north-south with short segments between
them; and the western third is a dozen small neighbourhoods of the same
shape. An up staircase is not a way down, and the number of them says
nothing about where the down one is.

## The decisions I would take back

1. **I should have checked the M map in the first ten decisions, not the
   fortieth.** Every positional mistake I made — reading the panel shift as
   a walk, walking east when I meant west — came from not knowing where I
   was on the level, and the M map settles that in one key.
2. **The first thirty decisions went to menus.** I sent `i`, then `e`, then
   a walk, and the walk was eaten by the equipment list because I did not
   remember that a screen which is not the map eats the next key. That
   cost three decisions and taught me the rule that is now in my notes.
3. **I got the keypad wrong three times** — 6 for west when 6 is east,
   8 for south when 8 is north — and each slip was invisible: the
   character moved, the turn counter moved, and the map looked plausible.
   The M map is what caught it. The digits are the only keys in this game
   that are not letters, and they are the only ones I had to look up
   three times in 141 decisions.
4. **I should have swept the southern rows first.** The western third of
   the level is entered from the level's southern edge, and I spent the
   first hundred decisions on the northern corridor and the eastern
   lattice before working out that the corridor along the north edge is
   sealed from the level below by vein walls. Two thirds of the budget
   went north; the reachable route west was south.
5. **I should have read the two scrolls when I picked them up** rather
   than carrying one unidentified scroll for eighty decisions, and I
   should have opened the chests by standing on them and pressing `o` and
   `5` instead of pressing `o` and a direction, which is what the manual
   says and what I did — and which worked; the chests were simply empty.
6. **The biggest thing I would do differently is not this life but the
   next one: a character that inherits no potion, no escape and no way
   home should spend its first decisions in the town buying the four
   things it will need, and should treat the staircase as the thing it
   will chase only when the kit is paid for.** I did not, because the
   character had 3 gold and the shops were 300 columns and three locked
   doors away.

## What I could not see or could not do

- **The western quarter of the level, columns 0 to 50.** It is a third of
  the dungeon's width and every row of it is unexplored, and it is not
  reachable from where I stood: the northern corridor ends in a pocket at
  column 78 and the southern rows are walled off from the middle. I did
  not find a way in in 145 decisions and I did not find one in the source
  either. The character finished at level column 50, the westernmost
  square any life of it has reached here.
- **I could not read my absolute position from the main map**, only from
  the M map, and the M map is a picture of remembered ground, so a small
  pocket of explored floor does not appear on it at all.
- **I never saw a `>` glyph in a main-map panel**, so I cannot say the
  staircase is not in the western third — only that it is not in the
  sixty-eight per cent I walked, and that the M map agrees.
- **I could not identify the two scrolls before reading them**, and the
  title of an unidentified object is not its kind: two scrolls with the
  same title turned out to be a Blessing and a Light.
- **I did not kill the monsters worth experience on purpose.** The level
  is quiet (`LF:1-1`) and what there is gives a quarter of a unit.

## Leads, with what would settle each

1. **Where is the down staircase of this level, and is the western third
   enterable at all?** The generator puts it on a square with exactly three
   adjacent walls, uniformly. **What would settle it:** a run that maps
   the level from the *western* end — that is, one that goes up to the
   town and comes down and then walks west along the southern rows, which
   is the only route I could not find.
2. **Does a level have more than one down staircase?** My notes said one;
   the source says `alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, 1, ...)` — one. This level
   had **three** up staircases, so the generator does allocate several of
   those, and the question is whether the down one is also plural.
   **What would settle it:** read `gen-cave.c` around the `alloc_stairs`
   calls for `FEAT_LESS` and `FEAT_MORE` and say what each asks for.
3. **Is the down staircase always at a dead end, and are dead ends
   common enough to be searched for?** `alloc_stairs` tries three adjacent
   walls first and then falls back to two, one and zero. **What would
   settle it:** count the dead ends on a level, and the number of them
   divided into the number of squares, which gives the chance that a
   random walk finds it.
4. **Does a depth-1 chest ever have anything in it?** Four said no on
   this level and one said no in the first life. **What would settle it:**
   read the chest placement code (`place_chest` in `gen-stairs.c` or
   `cave.c`) and see whether a depth-1 chest is generated with contents.
5. **What is the real relationship between the M map and the level?** My
   three lives disagreed and the source says it scales the whole level. The
   one thing I could not do is read the M map's scale exactly: 78 columns
   for 198 squares is 2.54 squares a column, so a single remembered
   staircase could be drawn over by a neighbouring tile. **What would
   settle it:** a run that finds a `>` in the western third and checks
   whether the M map shows it.
6. **Can a level-1 druid be made to level at all?** The formula says no.
   **What would settle it:** a run that kills twenty depth-1 small kobolds
   and counts the experience, which is the only way to be sure that the
   quarter-unit estimate is right and not an artefact of the integer
   division.

## End state

Alive, on depth 1 of seed 23, **character level 4**, 29/33 hit points, 7/7
spell points, armour class 12, 3 gold, 26 experience units to level 5.
Carrying a Book of Nature Magics [Lesser Charms] with Detect Life, Fox Form,
Remove Hunger and Stinking Cloud, 2 Rations of Food, 19 Flasks of oil, 4
Potions of Cure Light Wounds and a Cloak [1,+0]; the Wooden Torch is the
light source and is not in the pack. No scrolls, no Phase Door, no Recall.
The character stands at level column 50, row 9 — the westernmost square any
life of it has reached on this level — with a permanent light globe from a
Scroll of Light and 3 gold it cannot spend.

**Final turn 24,105, after 145 decisions and 6,824 turns of game time.**
